drafts.title: Clarifying llama.cpp HTTP server file upload: How does it combine file content with prompts?
drafts.body: A Reddit post from 2025 raises questions about how llama.cpp's HTTP server file upload feature integrates uploaded file content with user prompts. The original poster wonders if the file content is simply concatenated with the prompt text before being sent to the model. They used llama 3.2 3B Q4_K_S and tried asking questions about the uploaded file's contents. However, the responses were inconsistent—sometimes the model answered the question correctly, other times it seemed to interpret the file content itself rather than the query. This variability and the lack of clear documentation make it unclear how the file upload feature actually works under the hood. Has anyone here observed or figured out the exact mechanism by which the file upload and prompt are combined? Also, are there known strategies to improve reproducibility of answers when querying uploaded file contents through this interface? Understanding this would help in reliably leveraging the file upload button for local LLM use cases.

drafts.title: Exploring reproducibility challenges with llama.cpp HTTP server file upload queries
drafts.body: From a 2025 Reddit discussion, a user reports inconsistent outputs when querying the contents of files uploaded via llama.cpp’s HTTP server interface. They speculate the file content might be concatenated with the prompt, but this isn't confirmed. Using llama 3.2 3B Q4_K_S, they ran about 15 tests and found that sometimes questions about the file's contents were answered correctly, while other times the model seemed to focus on interpreting the file content itself rather than the query. The user also expressed a desire for reproducible results—getting the same answers when repeating the same prompts in new conversations. Given these observations and the unclear internal handling of file uploads, what approaches or best practices might help achieve more consistent and reproducible querying of uploaded files in llama.cpp’s HTTP server?

drafts.title: What does llama.cpp’s HTTP server file upload actually do, and how to get stable Q&A on file contents?
drafts.body: A 2025 Reddit post questions the actual function of the file upload button in llama.cpp’s HTTP server. The poster wonders if the uploaded file content is simply appended to their prompt text or handled differently. Using llama 3.2 3B Q4_K_S, they attempted to ask questions about the uploaded file’s contents but saw mixed results: sometimes the model answered correctly, other times it seemed to interpret the file content as the query itself. They want reproducible answers—consistent outputs when issuing the same prompts in new sessions—but the variability suggests the internal combination of file and prompt is not straightforward or stable. Does anyone have insight into how the file upload input is processed internally? Also, what techniques might improve reproducibility when querying uploaded files via this interface?
